New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo announced his retirement of a post-touchdown backflip celebration, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the change. Speaking at a Friday news conference, Harbaugh said he was 'happy' with the decision, that he supports it, and that he hopes Skattebo scores many touchdowns soon to prove himself on the field.

The move appears connected to recent injuries among players who perform acrobatic celebrations after sacks. Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in Munich during a Sunday game, with his right knee buckling as he landed from an airborne jump. The injury is described as the second season-ending one of Hutchinson's career and leaves a significant gap in the Lions' defense.

The text presents these statements as reported remarks attributed to Harbaugh rather than verified facts about Skattebo's reasoning or any formal policy adopted by the Giants.
items.title: Giants coach John Harbaugh backs Cam Skattebo's decision to retire backflip touchdown celebration

items.summary: The Japanese government is considering adding organic chemical products to its list of 'specified critical products' under the economic security promotion law, according to sources. The move aims to strengthen domestic supply chains for these chemicals—used in high-performance materials essential to semiconductor manufacturing and as raw materials (such as ethylene and propylene) for plastics—which are produced from naphtha. Discussions would begin at a closed-door expert panel, with plans to amend the relevant Cabinet order by the end of fiscal 2026. The proposal follows disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz caused by the U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran, which has raised concerns about stable supplies; Japan relies on Middle East imports for most petroleum used in naphtha production, while domestic chemical output declines and dependence on China grows. Under the existing system, designated products receive subsidies and other support to help private-sector companies maintain supply stability, alongside items such as semiconductors, storage batteries, and ventilators.
items.title: Japan Considers Adding Organic Chemicals to Critical Products List

items.summary: Max Verstappen won the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday, November 21, taking his fourth win of the season and his third victory at this event within four years. The race featured 35 lead changes over its 50 laps under floodlights, with drivers running nose-to-tail and track advantage shifting repeatedly between straight sections. Verstappen beat McLaren's Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds to win from pole position; teammate Oscar Piastri finished third after starting 17th. Both Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collected 10-second penalties for separate incidents, finishing seventh and tenth respectively. Mercedes' George Russell hit the barriers late in the race and dropped to ninth, while Antonelli took fourth ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly (fifth) and teammate Franco Colapinto (sixth). Carlos Sainz finished eighth at Williams in his 250th Grand Prix.
items.title: Verstappen wins Las Vegas Grand Prix for third time in four years

items.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) searched the residence on Friday of Luvkush Kumar, a Superintendent of the Haryana CGST posted in Sector 25, Panchkula, and recovered assets reportedly worth about ₹1.86 crore after arresting him for allegedly accepting a bribe. The seizure included Indian currency notes valued at ₹24.29 lakh and foreign currency notes at ₹15.65 lakh; gold and silver bullion plus jewellery estimated at ₹1.46 crore, which together with the cash brought the total to roughly ₹1.86 crore. Investigators also found documents covering six bank accounts, investment portfolios, life insurance policies, several immovable properties, vehicle ownership records for Kumar and family members, and financial transaction logs. Kumar was caught after a trap operation following a complaint from a businessman who said he had been asked for illegal gratification in connection with GST proceedings against his firm, including avoiding heavy penalties and issuing further demand notices. CBI spokesperson Beena Yadav stated that the accused initially demanded ₹50 lakh, which during negotiations fell to ₹20 lakh before being raised again to ₹25 lakh, at which point Kumar agreed to accept a ₹10 lakh first instalment with the remainder payable later; she said preliminary verification corroborated this demand. The CBI registered an FIR after the complaint and is conducting further investigation.
items.title: ₹1.86 crore in cash and gold seized from Panchkula CGST officer arrested over ₹10 lakh bribe

Following the November 3 midterm elections, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill told EL PAÍS that while her party is in its strongest position in decades due to unity, it faces a pressing challenge as it prepares to take control of Congress in January: acting decisively and quickly. She argued that voters are cynical and struggling, so Democrats must 'move fast and show wins right away' before public trust can be restored. Sherrill attributed the party's success to its focus on affordability, noting that cost-of-living concerns were a decisive issue for voters who cited Trump's handling of the economy as their main concern; she described campaigns built around fixing rent and utility costs as more compelling than those running on abstract themes like fascism or democratic institutions. She framed this approach as lessons learned from recent victories by figures such as Zohran Mamdani in New York City and Abigail Spanberger in Virginia, which became the party's model.

Sherrill explained that her sense of urgency stems from her military background: she graduated from flight school at the United States Naval Academy in the first class of women qualified for combat operations, served as a pilot in Europe and the Middle East over nine years, then studied law to become a federal prosecutor. She entered politics during Trump's first presidency when Democrats took control of Congress in 2018, and she helped flip two congressional seats in New Jersey this November while campaigning for Democratic governors-elect Gina Hinojosa (Texas) and Amy Acton (Ohio).

On party unity, Sherrill dismissed debates over factions as artificial. She characterized the idea that Democrats are 'ungovernable' due to internal divisions as flawed, arguing one person cannot embody all of American identity—comparing it to rejecting a monarchy—and noting Trump considers himself a king. Although she belongs to the moderate and pragmatic wing, she acknowledged sharing some views with progressives on immigration: while she has not called for abolishing ICE like Mamdani did, New Jersey banned immigration agents from covering their faces during enforcement operations (prompting an ongoing lawsuit by the Trump administration), Sherrill sought to limit the agency's activities in her state and demanded the closure of Delaney Hall detention center in Newark. She cited at least three deaths among detainees after a month-long hunger strike last summer.

Looking ahead, Sherrill said she views New Jersey as a roadmap for Democrats over Trump's final two years in office and into 2028, when the Democratic nominee will face Trump's successor since he cannot run again. She expressed interest in seeing leadership resembling her own approach but declined to run herself despite having military veteran, former prosecutor, and former Congress member credentials; she noted receiving calls about a potential candidacy though her name is not on contender lists.

Her record includes signing legislation curbing algorithmic rent pricing, laws restricting state and local cooperation with federal anti-immigration efforts, and winning a lawsuit to secure federal funding for the New Jersey–New York rail tunnel. She emphasized that when Trump acts illegally there should be no negotiation—only court action—and argued people now reject government inefficiency after witnessing how quickly he dismantled things, so effective service requires rebuilding rapidly.
items.title: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill Urges Democrats to Act Quickly After Midterm Gains

items.summary: Jason Horne-Francis, Port Adelaide's coach, says he is prepared to recruit off-contract Western Australian player Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera into the team during next year's State of Origin (AFL Origin) camp. The recruitment would require a change in state affiliation, as Wanganeen-Milera currently represents South Australia alongside Callum Wilkie, Jordan Dawson and Lachie Neale to form that state's first five players. For Western Australia, the first five named were Patrick Cripps, Charlie Cameron, Kysaiah Pickett, Luke Jackson and Tom Barrass. The item was published on 3 September following a final score of Dockers 40, Hawks 72.
items.title: Horne-Francis prepared to recruit Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera during AFL Origin camp

items.summary: India posted its highest team total on New Zealand soil, declaring at 9/720 in the first innings of a Test in Wellington. Centuries from KL Rahul (136) and Rishabh Pant (128) produced a 352-run lead over New Zealand after India reached 8/341 all out before its declaration; the final score was IAW 6/338 against AAW 8/341. The innings fell 39 runs short of India's all-time highest Test total, which is 7-759 recorded against England in 2016.
items.title: India set New Zealand Test record with declaration at 9-720 in Wellington

items.summary: A Madeira Ocean Expedition conducted throughout October by more than 200 specialists, organized by the regional government with partners including the Oceano Azul Foundation, National Geographic Pristine Seas, ARDITI, and Oceanário de Lisboa, completed nearly 500 dives, lowered more than 300 baited cameras, filtered seawater for DNA traces, mapped shorelines with drones, and sampled microplastics to assess marine health. Early results indicate the region's fully protected areas are functioning: limpets were larger and more abundant inside reserves where collection is limited, large groupers occurred there too, and the Mediterranean monk seal population—reduced to six to eight animals by the late 1980s after the Desertas Islands became a reserve in 1990—is now increasing slowly. The expedition also recorded the first-ever satellite tagging of a Blainville's beaked whale in the North-East Atlantic, with early data showing it favoring waters south of the Desertas near fully protected areas. A notable concern was that fewer than 10 sharks were recorded across the entire survey, which organizers describe as concerning and consistent with wider Atlantic shark declines. The expedition operated from the tall ship Santa Maria Manuela and smaller boats around Madeira, Porto Santo, and the Desertas Islands; drift cameras reached depths of 1,060 metres, revealing sponge fields and large black corals possibly several hundred years old alongside lost fishing gear. By area, most of Madeira is deep sea, which researchers note makes study difficult. Findings will inform decisions on managing and expanding marine protected areas as the region works toward protecting 30 per cent of its seas by 2030 with at least 10 per cent fully protected; a second expedition planned for 2027 aims to explore deeper waters.
items.title: Madeira Ocean Expedition Finds Marine Reserves Working but Shark Populations Concerningly Low

items.summary: Euronews Business examined which European countries are best prepared for a skills-first hiring approach, using the OECD's Skills-First Readiness and Adoption Index. The index scores each country on a 0 to 1 scale based on how well it identifies, develops, recognizes, and rewards skills through adult learning, use of skills data, public support for training, and employer valuation of demonstrated abilities. Sweden leads Europe with a score of 0.70, followed by France (0.69), the UK (0.65), Belgium (0.64), Finland (0.63), Czechia (0.61), Norway (0.61), and Latvia (0.61). The average across 23 European countries is 0.58, with Spain, Denmark, Portugal, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, and Austria near that level; Germany (0.57), Switzerland (0.57), and the Netherlands (0.56) slightly below it. Hungary (0.45) and Greece (0.46) record the lowest scores, while Turkey (0.52), Slovakia (0.54), and Slovenia (0.54) also score low. OECD senior economist Glenda Quintini noted that lower-scoring countries typically face greater barriers related to adult learning participation and broader learning ecosystems, so the gap reflects how effectively nations identify, develop, recognize, and reward skills rather than education systems alone. The US scores 0.60, slightly above Europe's average, while Canada (0.55), Japan (0.51), and South Korea (0.48) fall below it. Centre for Skills-First Practices director Soon-Joo Gog emphasized that most European countries have laid foundations but must make these practices routine through coordinated effort across the system.
items.title: OECD Skills-First Readiness Index Ranks Sweden Highest in Europe While Degrees Remain a Valued Signal

items.summary: The article frames the U.S. midterm elections as a milestone in the country's long fight against injustice, juxtaposing them with cultural works that have chronicled American racism and coexistence—John Ford's The Searchers (1956), Cheyenne Autumn (1964), Elvis Presley's In the Ghetto, and Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird. The central event is Texas producing one of the midterms' biggest surprises: for the first time in 30 years the Democrats won a Senate seat, ending Republican dominance under President Donald Trump, while electing Gina Hinojosa as its first Hispanic governor. Other election "firsts" cited include openly gay senator Chris Pappas; Muslim senator Abdul El-Sayed (targeted by racist slurs from Trump and the MAGA movement); Georgia's first Black governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms; Ohio's first Jewish governor, Amy Acton (also its first woman to govern that state); New Mexico's first Native American governor, Deb Haaland of the Laguna Pueblo tribe in a state where about 12% of the population is Indigenous; and Minnesota's first Native American lieutenant governor, Peggy Flanagan of the Ojibwe people. According to The Guardian, these gains included a record total of 180 elected Native candidates across local, state, and federal offices. The article notes that this diversity contrasts with Trump-era statements against the civil rights movement—including disparaging John Lewis's legacy—and reminds readers that Indigenous Americans did not gain full citizenship until 1924 or universal voting rights in every state until the 1960s. A stated limitation is that a long road remains ahead, even as these firsts are presented as evidence that justice can continue to move forward.
items.title: U.S. Midterm Elections Bring Record Diversity of Firsts Amid Ongoing Struggle Against Injustice

items.summary: According to a Wall Street Journal report, Kim Jong Un has not responded to contact attempts from President Donald Trump, while Pyongyang continues expanding its nuclear program and strengthening ties with Russia. Trump tried reaching Kim through established phone lines last year without response, then sent a letter that US officials delivered by hand at North Korea's UN mission in Manhattan before it was placed unopened before a US representative. During his recent Asia trip, renewed efforts to arrange face-to-face talks failed because Kim set conditions Washington could not accept; the administration had floated proposals including a possible formal end to the Korean War and an ambiguous statement on denuclearization, though officials said no meeting-brokering effort was underway as of Saturday. North Korea's arsenal reportedly grew from an estimated 20-30 warheads in 2019 to around 60, with Pyongyang developing solid-fuel ICBMs that can reach the US and are harder to track than liquid-fuel systems. The US intelligence community acknowledged Kim has no intention of negotiating away his weapons programs, and a Trump administration official said the White House lacks a detailed policy plan while leaving its North Korea special envoy position vacant—the national security strategy omitted North Korea for the first time since the Cold War ended. On economic grounds, North Korea's economy reportedly grew 3.5% last year (its third consecutive year above 3%), and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated North Korea was responsible for 89% of cryptocurrency hacking losses this year versus 15% in 2021, including a Binance heist exceeding $6 billion; Russia vetoed the renewal of UN sanctions monitoring in 2024 while China abstained. The report notes these developments are drawn from WSJ reporting and people familiar with matters rather than confirmed by direct sources.
items.title: Kim Jong Un Ignores Trump Contact Attempts as North Korea Expands Nuclear Arsenal

items.summary: The Network of Women in Media, India filed a rejoinder with the Supreme Court on Saturday challenging the Delhi Police's characterization of its actions during October protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The police had described their conduct—removing journalists from protest sites and placing them in vehicles—as crowd control or removal for verification rather than detention or arrest. The media organisation argued that personal liberty cannot be justified simply by refraining from labeling an action as detention, and contended that the right to newsgathering extends beyond accredited professionals with employer-issued identification cards to include independent, freelance, and digital journalists. It further asserted that recording police conduct at public protests constitutes protected newsgathering regardless of duration, format, or platform. Separately, the media organisation disputed the Delhi Police's closure of three women journalists' sexual harassment complaints, noting the force had determined allegations were uncorroborated based on two complainants declining to pursue their cases and CCTV footage showing no assault; it argued that an inquiry conducted by the accused personnel required independence and that a complainant's choice not to proceed does not establish that misconduct did not occur. The report attributes these claims to Live Law, which covered the filing, though specific details of any court ruling or final resolution are not stated in the source material.
items.title: Media Organisation Argues Delhi Police Cannot Frame Journalist Restraints as Crowd Control

items.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Friday as fears about artificial intelligence weighed on markets, driving the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 1.93% to 48,147.33, the S&P 500 down 3.70% to 6,910.39, and the Nasdaq Composite down 5.28% to 22,617.73 — pushing all three indexes into correction territory. The Nasdaq has now erased its entire year's gains and sits more than 18% below its October record close, while the S&P 500 and Dow are each more than 11% under their respective records. AI and chip stocks led the decline: Nvidia fell about 14%, Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, and Micron Technology dropped more than 12% each, and recently publicized Anthropic slid 8.5%. Richard Saperstein, chief investment officer at Treasury Partners, attributed investor reassessment to expectations of slower data center construction, fewer financing options for AI projects, and slower profit growth among technology firms; the selloff was further compounded by capital drawn away from other stocks due to the Anthropic listing, a stronger dollar tightening financial conditions, expectations of additional Federal Reserve rate hikes, and concerns that Democratic control of Congress after midterms could bring tighter regulation of the AI industry. Market anxiety rose sharply as the CBOE Volatility Index closed at 35.89, up 26.2%, while risk aversion spread to commodities with US gold futures falling 4.62% and silver plunging 7.41%. Several firms have warned that selling pressure may persist.
items.title: AI concerns push all three major US indexes into correction territory

items.summary: More than 100 children and 12 adults were hospitalised with suspected food poisoning after eating 'chowmein' (noodles) at a village fair held on Saturday evening in Hiri village, under the Kirnapur police station limits of Balaghat district in Madhya Pradesh. The incident was reported by several visitors who complained of acute stomach ache shortly after consuming the noodles, according to Balaghat Collector Aditya Singh. Initially, 118 children were admitted to the community health centre in Kirnapur; of these, 45 were shifted to the Balaghat district hospital for further treatment while the remaining 73 were discharged after receiving primary care. The 12 adults who fell ill were also admitted to the district hospital's medical ward. Officials confirmed on Sunday that all patients are stable and out of danger, with Chief Medical and Health Officer Dr Shatrughan Singh Dahiya stating they were being treated under doctor supervision. Collector Aditya Singh visited the hospital to check on the patients' condition and directed staff to ensure proper care. The report notes a related incident in which nearly 2,000 people fell ill from suspected food poisoning linked to Indonesia's free school meals program, though this is presented as an unrelated item rather than part of the Madhya Pradesh event.
items.title: Over 100 children hospitalised after suspected food poisoning from chowmein at a village fair in Madhya Pradesh

items.summary: Mexican authorities arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," a 44-year-old leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation (Los Mazatlecos) and one of the FBI's ten most-wanted fugitives, in a military operation near Guasave, Sinaloa. The capture followed years on the run; US agencies had offered a USD 5 million reward for information leading to his arrest, and he had been under indictment in the United States for more than 14 years.
items.title: Mexico captures FBI most-wanted drug lord El Chapo Isidro; cartel retaliation leaves 11 dead in Guasave

items.summary: A 50-year-old unidentified woman was sexually assaulted and murdered inside an unoccupied train coach at Nagercoil railway station in Tamil Nadu on 14 November, with her decomposed remains discovered four days later. Police used CCTV footage to arrest a 31-year-old suspect named Ayyappan. The incident has drawn attention to security deficiencies at railway station yards and the broader law-and-order situation in the state. Separately reported items include a case in Tuticorin, where a 16-year-old Class 11 student was killed following an argument with the accused who then attempted suicide while police investigate; Karnataka High Court granting default bail to Prajwal Revanna in an obscene video case though he remains detained on other convictions; and Prime Minister Modi touring West Bengal, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh promoting development initiatives. The source material is presented as unverified reporting.
items.title: Woman Sexually Assaulted and Murdered at Nagercoil Railway Station; Suspect Arrested via CCTV

items.summary: Following the October election, caretaker premier Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party was tasked with forming Israel's next government. Negotiations between Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu have stalled over who should hold the prime ministership, with reports indicating that Netanyahu remains firm on retaining the office for a full four-year term rather than accepting a rotational arrangement under which Eisenkot would initially serve as PM. Likud conveyed conditions for a possible national unity government through Hebrew media; AFP reported that these leave no room for such a rotation and extend beyond the prime ministership question, including demands for an administration of Jewish-led parties from far-right Otzma Yehudit to left-wing Democrats while excluding both Arab-led parties, plus calls to end personal attacks on Netanyahu, endorse another offensive against Iran, retain Israeli positions in Gaza until Hamas is removed, keep judicial overhaul legislation pending consensus, advance a Haredi military draft bill per the outgoing government's proposal, and hold a political commission of inquiry into the October 7 attack. Eisenkot invited Likud representatives for fresh talks beginning Sunday (November 22), which his party described as an effort to bring in the widest possible grouping; AFP reported this invitation. The three allegations concerning Likud's positions on judicial overhaul, military conscription, and the proposed inquiry have been rejected by Likud, though it did not address its remaining demands. Opposition leaders Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman have ruled out joining Netanyahu's camp or even a rotational arrangement that would let Netanyahu become PM after Eisenkot; Liberman advocated instead bringing ultra-Orthodox parties Shas and United Torah Judaism into the coalition to reach 61 seats for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. However, United Torah Judaism denied reports of negotiation progress while Shas showed little inclination to abandon its alliance with Likud. As an alternative if negotiations fail, Eisenkot could seek a minority government relying on abstention from Ra'am and the Joint List; Liberman rejected this possibility as potentially helping Netanyahu return to power. Eisenkot promised not to let talks drag indefinitely and said he was prepared to put a minority national emergency government to a Knesset vote if broader coalition efforts failed.
items.title: Netanyahu Rejects Rotational Arrangement as Likud Sets Conditions for Unity Government

items.summary: An official, speaking on condition of anonymity, stated that Tamil Nadu had signed memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with 112 companies committing investments worth ₹1,14,811 crore over the first 195 days since the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government took office in May. The official projected these commitments would generate approximately 1,32,771 jobs across sectors described as diversified for balanced growth. This announcement preceded a second investors' conclave scheduled for November 25 in Chennai, following the first round held on August 13; chief minister C Joseph Vijay was sworn in on May 10 after TVK won 108 of the assembly's 234 seats and formed a post-poll alliance with Congress, VCK, and IUML. In response to opposition concerns about transparency—particularly allegations that many MoUs were signed during the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) rule—the official said details are regularly shared through Guidance Tamil Nadu or the Chief Ministers' Office, citing a government commitment to accountability. However, BJP and other opposition figures questioned whether investments designated for Tamil Nadu were instead being diverted to Andhra Pradesh; former Puducherry lieutenant governor Tamilisai Soundararajan called on the state industries department to clarify retention measures for existing firms and disclose how many announced MoUs have become operational factories versus new job creation. The report notes these investment claims remain unverified, as no independent confirmation of the figures or their conversion into functioning enterprises was provided.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Reports ₹1.14 Lakh Crore in TVK-Era Investments Amid BJP Questions Over Andhra Diversion

items.summary: CCTV footage of a Saturday morning accident on a highway in Andhra Pradesh's Kakinada district shows an elderly man riding a motorcycle emerge from a service lane and attempt to cross directly into the path of an approaching blue SUV. The SUV driver swerved onto the opposite side of the road to avoid him, colliding head-on with an oncoming white SUV; that impact triggered a chain reaction in which another motorcyclist was thrown several feet into the air. According to the report, two people died and three others were seriously injured and rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment. The identities of both the deceased and the injured have not yet been ascertained, and further details are pending.
items.title: Two Killed in Chain-Reaction Crash on Kakinada Highway After SUV Swerves from Elderly Motorcyclist

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar offered to constitute a five-member inquiry committee chaired by BJP state president BY Vijayendra to examine the expenditure on renovating the Kumara Krupa guest house, which was converted into his official residence 'Ganga.' The offer followed Vijayendra's accusation that approximately Rs 100 crore of public money had been spent on the project and allegations that it was carried out without a proper tender process. Shivakumar stated the committee could include members from the BJP, JD(S), and Independents but would not require any Congress member, noting Vijayendra could select MLAs or MLCs within two days. He said the report could be submitted for Assembly discussion during the legislature session early next month. The proposal was made after Vijayendra's Friday questioning of extravagant spending during a drought and requests for clarification on reports that contractors had been instructed to submit bills totalling only Rs 2-3 crore.
items.title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar Offers BJP-Led Committee To Probe Kumara Krupa Renovation Cost

items.summary: Two people of Indian origin were shot dead in a Walmart parking lot in Surrey, British Columbia, on November 15. The victims, identified by the Surrey Police Service as 23-year-old Gaganpreet (Garry) Rehal and 24-year-old Sukhjeet Kaur—who lived in neighbouring Delta—were found with gunshot wounds at around 10:38 pm; first responders attempted resuscitation before both were pronounced dead. The Surrey Police Service stated that investigators believe the shooting was a targeted attack linked to organised crime, according to the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT). A red Mustang with its windows blown out was seen in the parking lot by CBC News reporter, and Rehal had prior weapons offences on record while Kaur reportedly had limited known contacts in Canada. Police believe a nearby car fire reported about 13 minutes after the shooting is connected to the killings, with the burnt vehicle considered possibly belonging to the suspect; this attribution was described as believed rather than confirmed. The IHIT said it is investigating the circumstances of the deaths and identifying those responsible, and has appealed for public assistance including CCTV footage and dash camera recordings. All details regarding motive, criminal affiliation, and the identity or role of any suspects remain unconfirmed pending further investigation.
items.title: Indian-Origin Couple Killed in Surrey, Canada; Organised Crime Link Suspected

items.summary: On Tuesday, MS Dhoni announced that he was ending his playing career in the Indian Premier League (IPL), an outcome described by the author as little surprising given the trajectory of his international and franchise careers. Dhoni debuted internationally in 2004 and led India to three ICC titles—the 2007 World Twenty20, the 2011 Cricket World Cup, and the 2013 Champions Trophy—before being inducted into the sport's Hall of Fame in 2025. He had already retired from Test cricket in 2014 and from other international formats by 2020, but remained active for six years playing franchise cricket exclusively for the Chennai Super Kings (CSK), whom he joined when the league began in 2008; CSK is regarded as arguably the most successful IPL franchise under his captaincy. The author's central criticism—that Dhoni retired too late and after recent struggles, leaving a 'bitter taste'—is explicitly framed as an unpopular personal view rather than established fact. Supporting context includes Dhoni being among the oldest cricketers in the IPL, playing for CSK despite squad transitions under Ravindra Jadeja and Ruturaj Gaikwad not panning out, his 2025 statement that he could play 'for as long as I want' even if injured or in a wheelchair, and his subsequent season (at age 44) during which he remained part of the squad but did not play at all due to injuries. The author notes Dhoni will continue with CSK as team mentor, similar to Sachin Tendulkar's role for the Mumbai Indians. No chart is warranted because the text contains no quantified comparison or trend suitable for visualization.
items.title: MS Dhoni Announces Retirement from IPL After 17 Years as a Player

items.summary: This morning briefing from Nov. 22, 2026 summarizes the day's top news across diplomacy, regional security, and general headlines. On diplomacy, US President Donald Trump said Saturday he intends to secure a "permanent" deal with Iran, insisting that no future American president should be able to allow Tehran to obtain a nuclear weapon; his stated goal is ensuring the agreement remains binding even if an incompetent president takes office in four, 15, or 20 years. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Saturday that Ankara's policy as a member of the Mecca Defense Alliance—along with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan—prioritizes defending Saudi Arabia, while confirming officials have not yet decided on deploying troops to Yemen; he also noted a potential US-Iran agreement carries critical weight for easing global economic strain beyond reopening the Strait of Hormuz. On regional security, UNIFIL has begun handing over some positions in southern Lebanon to the Lebanese army, with mission chief Diodato Abagnara stressing the importance of avoiding any security vacuum after the mandate ends on Dec. 31 and saying its core work—monitoring violations, providing humanitarian aid, protecting civilians, and supporting communities—should continue. General headlines include protesters marching through London demanding tighter AI regulation near BBC offices and Downing Street; India's Congress youth wing protesting outside Meta offices in Hyderabad and Mumbai over the BJP government's orders; restoration teams clearing around 420 meters (1,378 feet) of tunnels beneath Istanbul's Hagia Sophia Mosque, identifying six underground spaces and nine tunnels possibly dating to the Roman era; Real Madrid winning 2-1 over Celta Vigo to level on points with Barcelona in LaLiga; Leeds United beating Chelsea 4-1 in the Premier League; and Galatasaray winning all three points while Fenerbahce settled for a draw in the Turkish Super Lig. The briefing presents these as reported statements and results without independent verification of their accuracy.
items.title: Morning Briefing for Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026

items.summary: During the first Test between India and New Zealand, wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant made a remark captured on his stump microphone that went viral among fans. The comment—"Yahan se nahi aayega single… She is ready to mingle" (translated as "You won't get a single from here... she's ready to mingle")—appeared to be an observation suggesting the batter could not score off a particular fielding position, combined with a playful English phrase. The text attributes Pant's trademark style of mixing Hindi commentary with punchlines and his animated presence behind the stumps as context for the remark. It notes that this is consistent with prior viral instances of his stump mic chatter, including motivational comments to bowlers and attempts to unsettle opposition batters, though it offers no specific dates or match details beyond identifying the contest as India vs New Zealand. The piece frames Pant's remarks as entertainment value rather than substantive cricketing analysis.
items.title: Rishabh Pant's Stump Mic Remark Goes Viral During India vs New Zealand Test

items.summary: Scientists warn that El Nino-driven sea level rise and king tides are bringing a triple threat of heavy rain, rising seas and high surf to the California coastline this week. The US National Weather Service issued storm warnings on Thursday for dynamic fronts producing rainfall rates over an inch (25.4 mm) per hour, prompting multiple flash flood warnings. An atmospheric river affected by what is being called a super El Nino caused flooding in San Francisco on Wednesday, dumping 2.64 inches of rain in one day and surpassing a record that had stood for more than a century; the storm stranded cars on Bay Area freeways and left more than 51,000 electricity customers without power by Wednesday afternoon. El Nino is described as a climate pattern marked by warmer-than-normal tropical Pacific waters that can bring wetter conditions to California while temporarily raising sea levels along the West Coast, allowing high tides and powerful waves to reach farther inland. Large swells battered Southern California's coast on Thursday, worsening erosion from earlier storms; in October a 360-foot crack appeared in a coastal bluff beneath Pacific Coast Highway near Crystal Cove State Park, prompting Caltrans to restrict traffic to one lane each direction while crews stabilized the slope. A high surf advisory remained in effect for Malibu and Los Angeles County beaches through 9 a.m. Friday with waves of 6 to 9 feet expected. Scientists expect the worst next week when king tides run from Sunday through November 27, potentially accompanied by large swells and further rain; starting Monday maximum coastal water levels in parts of Southern California could exceed 8 feet. Mark Merrifield, director of the Center for Climate Change Impacts and Adaptation at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, warned that California faces a triple threat from higher waves, more rain and higher sea levels associated with this El Nino event. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration estimates roughly a 60 percent probability through October to December of a historic El Nino exceeding every prior event since records began in 1950, while the US Geological Survey states the event is projected to be the largest and most intense on record. In response, Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on October 27 establishing a Highway 1 Task Force to identify vulnerable sections of the coastal highway; emergency project expenditures along Big Sur totalled about $312 million from 2020 through 2026. The article notes it was auto-generated from an agency feed and unedited by FPJ's editorial team.
items.title: El Nino Drives Record Rainfall, King Tides And High Surf Along California Coast

items.summary: On Sunday, November 22 at approximately 6 PM, Uttar Pradesh authorities will run a coordinated mock drill across all 75 districts of the state to test emergency response readiness. Organized by the UP Civil Defence Department in accordance with Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) guidelines, Principal Secretary Samyukta Samaddar stated that District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), police, fire services, and the health department will participate. The exercise aims to assess warning systems and evaluate how quickly relevant departments, emergency services, and civil defence volunteers can respond during crises such as war or aerial strikes. Residents may hear air raid sirens lasting nearly two minutes followed by a temporary power blackout while they practice moving to safe locations and taking shelter; an all-clear signal will follow once the simulated threat ends. Samaddar emphasized that residents were informed in advance specifically to prevent panic and curb rumours, consistent with messages shared on social media platforms such as Zee Uttar Pradesh Uttarakhand's Twitter account dated November 22, 2026.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh to conduct statewide civil defence blackout and siren drill on November 22

items.summary: In the early hours of Sunday, November 22, 2026, a vehicle carrying pilgrims returning from Khatu Shyam Temple collided with a parked truck near Shambhupura on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan, killing nine people and injuring several others. According to Additional District Collector Rajesh Joshi, who spoke to ANI, the vehicle was transporting 16 members of one family heading back to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam; all nine deceased were from that same family. Authorities reported that post-mortem examinations are underway for those killed while injured persons receive medical care. A survivor recounted that the group had split into two vehicles en route toward Dhar, and upon receiving a phone call about the crash they rushed to the scene where three vehicles and 36 people were present; this account is not independently corroborated by officials. The article provides no official cause of the collision or details on how many injured survived.
items.title: Nine Pilgrims Killed When Vehicle Hits Parked Truck on Kota-Udaipur Highway in Rajasthan

items.summary: In an NPR interview, military analyst Phillips O'Brien argued that this week's summits—Trump meeting with Russian President Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China while European leaders gathered separately in Berlin to support Zelenskyy—demonstrated that the United States has grown closer to Russia than to Ukraine or its allies. He stated that U.S. policy now aims to pressure Ukraine into ceding territory, leaving Europe as Ukraine's sole source of military and financial aid; O'Brien characterized European capacity as strong materially but strategically dependent on American guidance. On the battlefield, he described a Russian strategy focused on breaking Ukrainian civilian will through daily attacks—such as strikes on Zelenskyy's hometown—and attributed weakened Ukrainian air defenses to U.S. restrictions on weapons plus interference with Starlink and Starshield systems that reportedly downed drones. He said Ukraine is instead attempting to cut supply lines into occupied Crimea, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia. Regarding Jared Kushner's proposal of 'NATO-like' security guarantees as a path to ending the war, O'Brien dismissed it as vague and argued the Trump administration is pushing for a deal by January 3 out of concern over Democratic control of Congress rather than because Putin would accept such terms. He added that Ukraine believes the war favors its side but feels undermined by American disengagement. All assessments reflect O'Brien's analysis; NPR noted transcript accuracy may vary and that audio remains authoritative.
items.title: Military Analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe Being Excluded from Trump's Russia-China Summits

items.summary: Toyota unveiled the BKE Concept, a small folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation. The design reportedly folds in around 30 seconds and becomes small enough to fit inside the trunk of Toyota's GR86 sports car. It was presented alongside other vehicles under the newly revived Scion brand, which Toyota is positioning less as its former youth-oriented car line and more as an experimental mobility laboratory it calls a 'freedom lab.' Although Toyota refers to the BKE as an electric bike, the vehicle has no pedals, meaning it would not qualify as an electric bicycle in Europe or North America; instead it falls into the broader category that includes scooters and motorcycles, making it essentially a small seated e-scooter. Toyota states the concept has been under development for several years by a small team of chassis and electrical engineers using real-world testing and feedback. Chairman Akio Toyoda reportedly participated in testing, with one reported change being an enlarged rear fender after he complained about getting splashed through puddles at the 2025 Japan Mobility Show. Toyota highlights camping, errands, last-mile transportation, and use as a pit bike alongside a GR86, noting the vehicle can be recharged from 110V AC outlets found in many Toyota vehicles so the carrying car acts as its charging station. The stated goal is to make short-distance mobility easier by matching smaller vehicles to shorter trips, which Toyota says could reduce emissions.
items.title: Toyota Unveils BKE Concept Folding Electric Two-Wheeler as Compact Companion Vehicle

items.summary:
Following Democrats' decisive victory in the US midterm elections, several Silicon Valley executives who had made hard-right political pivots during Donald Trump's second term are retreating toward more moderate or left-leaning positions. Elon Musk publicly downgraded his allegiance at a New York Times DealBook conference on Wednesday, telling an audience he was "not sure what Maga means" and calling himself "foolish" for spending roughly $500m to help elect Republicans in the midterms; he also characterized Texas Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa as moderate. Alex Karp of Palantir softened his previously hardline immigration stance, telling Politico that President Trump mishandled enforcement, and broadened this retreat by asserting that all of Palantir's products are essentially progressive despite the company's work powering ICE. Meta is reportedly shifting left after promoting a more bipartisan executive slate following the departure of Joel Kaplan, who had been promoted at the start of the Trump administration for his Republican ties.

The article notes these leaders previously maneuvered with political tides—Musk having donated to Democrats and celebrated LGBTQ+ workplace equality in 2018 before moving to Texas and funding Republicans—and frames Palantir as unusually embedded in controversial government work. Lesley Nash of Just Futures Law characterized Karp's public concerns about immigration enforcement as falling short, arguing that private expressions of doubt cannot mitigate the harm caused by a system his company enabled; she called for corporate accountability regarding complicity with Trump administration policies.

The text presents these shifts without independent verification and offers no quantitative data on the scale or financial impact of the political pivots. It also notes Palantir's long history dating to an ICE contract in 2011, its $30m Immigration OS contract under the second Trump administration, and claims by former employee Juan Sebastián Pinto that the company uses public statements to appeal to whoever controls government contracts.
items.title: Silicon Valley tech leaders retreat from right-wing politics after Democratic midterm gains

The Mantsinen 200 is a Finnish-built electric material handler designed for port and rail terminal operations, featuring tank treads that allow it to move around a worksite independently. The machine combines reach and lifting capacity with self-propelled mobility on its tracks.

Powering the unit is a 380 kW (~510 hp) grid-connected electric motor running at 1,800 rpm, drawing power from a standard 460V electrical connection, though other voltage options are available to suit local site requirements. Mantsinen states that its electrically powered machines deliver the same performance as diesel counterparts while eliminating exhaust emissions and reducing operating noise, energy consumption, and maintenance costs.

The machine uses a load-sensing hydraulic system with four variable-displacement piston pumps and a separate closed-loop swing circuit. It also incorporates the proprietary HybriLift energy-recovery system, which Mantsinen claims improves energy efficiency by up to 50%—effectively providing an additional ~300 hp of lifting assistance at average lifting speed by capturing potential energy as the boom is lowered and storing it in hydraulic accumulators for reuse during subsequent lifts.

An optional diesel-powered PowerPack allows operators to disconnect from the main power supply while still traveling around a worksite with basic hydraulic functions, though Mantsinen notes a battery-backed version could be developed. The text presents these specifications as manufacturer claims without independent verification.
items.title: Mantsinen 200 Electric Material Handler Uses Tank Treads for Port and Rail Terminal Operations

items.summary: A new report by the think tank Policy Exchange, titled 'The China Trap,' argues that Britain's transition to net zero has shifted into the hands of a state it characterizes as hostile. The report cites data showing China accounts for 91 percent of UK solar imports, 94 percent of permanent magnets used in wind power, and roughly 70 percent of global battery production used in electric vehicles. It also flags that China imposed export controls while Royal Navy drone boats were reportedly transmitting data to Chinese internet addresses, framing the clean energy market dominance as a tool of economic statecraft. The report warns these supply chain dependencies expose critical sectors such as energy and Britain's £40bn automotive export industry to risk. Shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat responded by accusing the government of 'capitulation,' stating it had swapped carbon dependency in the Middle East for solar panels from China, while Labour peer Maurice Glasman called uncoupling from China strategically vital for British sovereignty. Defence secretary Wes Streeting defended the government's approach ahead of Chinese counterpart Admiral Dong Jun's visit to London, arguing that climate change does not respect ideological boundaries and that no credible global response can succeed without China's participation as both the world's largest greenhouse gas emitter and greatest producer of renewable energy technologies; his remarks drew on Labour manifesto wording calling for cooperation where possible, competition where needed, and challenge where necessary. The report was published shortly before a trilateral meeting between President Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin, which reportedly agreed to reform the United Nations, increase fuel production, limit international courts' jurisdiction, and prevent nuclear war.
items.title: Policy Exchange Report Warns UK Net Zero Transition Depends on China, Drawing 'Capitulation' Criticism

items.summary: Route 62 is a roughly 850 km road trip that runs from Cape Town in the Western Cape to Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) in the Eastern Cape, marketed as one of the world's longest wine routes. The route links valleys, mountain passes, villages with mineral hot springs, fruit orchards, ostrich farms, and the Cango Caves. It originated as an 18th-century ox-wagon and trade route connecting historic farming towns near the Cape and in the semi-desert Klein Karoo with the two coastal cities; after the N2 east-coast highway was completed in 1958, much of the through traffic left these settlements quiet for decades. Tourism along the retained old road revived from the post-apartheid 1990s onward. Tourists and tourism managers describe the drive as a slow-paced journey that emphasizes interaction with locals and scenic winding roads between mountains and green valleys, rather than speed. Oudtshoorn is noted as having gained prosperity around 1864 when ostrich feathers became fashionable in Europe, and remains central to the town's tourism identity today.
items.title: South Africa's Route 62: an 850 km wine-route drive between Cape Town and Gqeberha

items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned on Saturday an alleged assassination attempt against a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, which she described as 'an attack on EU soil' and called unacceptable. Von der Leyen stated the EU stands in full solidarity with Denmark and all member states targeted by Russian hybrid attacks, though no proof of the plot was provided beyond the allegation that it was orchestrated by Russian intelligence services. The Russian embassy in Copenhagen said Friday that the accusations were not backed with proof. Separately, von der Leyen indicated the EU would soon propose a new European Security Strategy to reinforce preparedness and deterrence. Denmark urged member states to take concrete actions against Moscow after authorities announced the foiled plot; according to a message sent on Friday evening to senior European diplomats—seen by Reuters and confirmed by two diplomats—the bloc should impose further restrictions on Russian nationals' access to the Schengen zone, including halting tourist visas for Russian citizens and adopting a Schengen-wide policy of non-recognition of Russian non-biometric passports. Denmark was set to present these proposals at a meeting of EU ambassadors in Brussels on Monday. The article also references an unrelated proposal that the EU would offer a new €45 billion Ukraine loan to be repaid by Russia, which is not connected to the assassination allegation.
items.title: EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark

Global Voices interviewed Pratistha Gautam in November 2026 as part of coverage tied to the UN's 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, which runs from November 25 to December 10, 2026. The interview highlights a broader framing that survivors across South Asia continue to struggle accessing social or legal justice despite growing global recognition of gender-based violence. Gautam reported being sexually abused by her close maternal uncle for four days when she was 11 years old; after the abuse ended on the fifth day, neighbors helped her escape and lock herself in a room while screaming until they responded. She attributes surviving to having witnessed men mistreating women without indifference growing up.

The article places Gautam's experience within regional context, citing high-profile unsolved cases in Nepal — 13-year-old Nirmala Panta found dead in a sugarcane field since 2018 and 3-year-old Garima found dead inside an abandoned house in Jeetpur. It also cites a World Health Organization report estimating that nearly one in three women worldwide (31.6 percent, roughly 840 million) have experienced physical or sexual violence in their lifetime.

Gautam now lives in Adelaide, South Australia, where she has complex PTSD and works as a mental health clinician providing pro bono counseling to abuse survivors while collaborating with Rakshya Nepal on protecting women and girls from exploitation and trafficking. She describes ongoing symptoms including nightmares, panic attacks when viewing sexual-abuse material, dissociation, insomnia, trust issues toward men, relationship difficulties that led to divorce, and the view that she would have difficulty living a normal life.

The piece notes social stigma around abuse in South Asia rooted in ideas of "purity," and references Nepal's gendered sayings — "timi ta chori manche ho ni" (you are a girl) and "chora manche vayera gari halchan ni" (boys will be boys). The article is grounded entirely in Gautam's account as reported to Global Voices; the statistics cited come from external sources, not her testimony.
items.title: Pratistha Gautam: From Childhood Sexual Abuse in Nepal to Mental Health Advocacy

items.summary: The U.K. government aims to accelerate nuclear power development as part of its decarbonisation strategy, planning to complete an overhaul of nuclear regulations by the end of 2027. The reforms seek to reduce licensing bureaucracy while maintaining safety standards, targeting a reduction in reactor design approval time from around three or four years to two years. These changes support broader goals of quadrupling nuclear output to 24 GW by 2050 and meeting an anticipated rise in energy demand of about 40 per cent by 2035. The push follows the March government statement linking Middle East events to the need for clean homegrown power, as well as the September 2025 U.K.-U.S. Atlantic Partnership for Advanced Nuclear Energy agreement that allows shared regulatory assessments and is expected to ease participation for firms such as Holtec, TerraPower, Westinghouse, X-energy, EDF, Rolls-Royce SMR, and BWX Technologies. Specific projects include France's EDF developing the 3.2 GW Hinkley Point C and Sizewell C plants, £65.6 million in government investment across seven research programmes, $3.4 billion over four years for the Rolls-Royce SMR programme, and the Gwyndod project at Wylfa targeting 70 per cent U.K.-sourced content. However, a limitation is that only 10 of 47 Nuclear Regulatory Taskforce recommendations had been implemented as reported by the Centre for British Progress in September, suggesting the government would need to accelerate its review process to meet the end-of-2027 deadline.
items.title: U.K. Plans Nuclear Regulatory Overhaul by End of 2027

The Moroccan Royal Cabinet announced on Wednesday that King Mohammed has allocated 4 billion dirhams (€366 million) from the Hassan II Fund for Economic and Social Development to launch a national defence industry roadmap with 2035 as its target year. The plan's three stated goals are to create roughly 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, meet 40% of the Royal Armed Forces' and security services' equipment needs through domestic production by 2035, and generate more than 65% of defence-industry revenues from exports. Implementation is structured around a new strategic agency to carry out national defence industry policy and support investors, an industrial holding company to organize the production ecosystem and mobilize public and private capital, and two new defence-manufacturing zones in Ben Guerir and Benslimane—added to existing zones in Nouaceur and Sidi Yahya. The strategy draws on Morocco's automotive, aviation, and electronics expertise across priority areas including drones and autonomous systems, land and naval systems, defence electronics, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and dual-use technologies.

The roadmap is supported by international partnerships: Tata Advanced Systems (India) is cooperating to manufacture WhAP 8×8 armoured vehicles in Berrechid with a goal of increasing locally produced components; domestic firm MMI manufactures military turrets and remotely controlled weapon systems as an initial production base; and the Emirati group EDGE signed two agreements at the October Marrakech Air Show—one memorandum exploring local manufacturing of small arms and aircraft engines, and another covering supply of Desert Sting 16 and Thunder P-31 guided munitions to the Royal Moroccan Air Force. The king also directed establishment of a specialised academy for advanced training in partnership with industrial companies, plus a talent-channeling programme adapting vocational training to engineering, electronics, and digital needs.

As context, Stockholm International Peace Research Institute data place Morocco among Africa's leading importers of major weapon systems. No limitations or caveats were stated beyond these figures.
items.title: Morocco allocates €366 million toward a national defence-industry roadmap targeting 2035

items.summary: According to CleanTechnica, Ford has begun producing its own lithium iron phosphate (LFP) prismatic battery cells at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan facility, marking what it describes as the first delivery of LFP batteries in the U.S. for mainstream consumer automotive use. The initial shipment is headed to Louisville Assembly Plant to power Ford Fathom prototypes. CleanTechnica reports that the assembly lines reportedly deliver 40 cells every minute, which it characterizes as among the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China; this figure and characterization are attributed to a source rather than independently verified in the text. items.summary: On Nov. 20, the Spanish government approved a royal decree establishing energy sustainability, environmental, resilience and digital sovereignty requirements for data centers, announced by Third Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Ecological Transition Sara Aagesen following a Council of Ministers meeting. The regulation responds to rapid growth in electricity demand from data centers and AI infrastructure: projects have secured grid access permits for 15 GW—6 GW on the transmission network and 9 GW on distribution networks—which represents nearly 40% of Spain's peak electricity demand, with an additional 20 GW awaiting grid access. These figures significantly exceed projections in Spain's 2024 Artificial Intelligence Strategy, which anticipated less than 4 GW of data center electricity demand by 2030. The decree revises the August proposal that first introduced the requirement for data centers to source at least 80% of their electricity from additional renewable generation; it raises the capacity threshold for main requirements from an initially proposed 1 MW to 10 MW and covers renewable procurement, energy and water efficiency, grid flexibility, resilience and digital sovereignty. Data centers must demonstrate that at least 80% of annual consumption is covered by on-site renewable generation or long-term power purchase agreements with new facilities, meet hourly matching requirements between electricity consumption and renewable generation phased to 2032, achieve class A standards under European PUE and WUE classifications, and reach a water target of 0.1 liters per kWh for the highest efficiency classification. Eligible facilities may follow a transitional compliance pathway subject to conditions including participation in demand reduction mechanisms, and grid access or connection rights can be tied to compliance with requirements that allow data centers to reduce demand or disconnect loads during congestion or system stress. The government estimates that without the regulation, data center expansion could add €5 billion annually to electricity costs and increase industrial consumer bills by 25%. Alongside the decree, the Council of Ministers approved an updated electricity transmission network development plan through 2030 with planned investment of €17.14 billion ($18.82 billion), which allocates grid capacity for 47.4 GW of new demand—14.9 GW industry, 12.4 GW renewable hydrogen, 9.3 GW data centers and 6 GW residential/urban development—and includes approximately 6,707 km of new transmission lines, upgrades across 8,164 km of existing lines, and 193 substations.
items.title: Spain approves data center rules mandating 80% renewable electricity

items.summary: In October, China's electric vehicle market share reached a record 68%, as high gasoline prices combined with a wave of new battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) drove overall sales down 27% year over year to roughly 1.6 million units. The decline was concentrated in internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, which fell 44% YoY, while pure BEV share rose to 40% and plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) share held at 23%; combining these two categories yielded the record 68% of all cars sold with a plug. The author projects that if this trend continues, China could reach full electrification by 2030 and be entirely BEV before 2035, estimating final 2026 EV share above 60% with BEVs alone north of 40%. This pace would push the overall top-10 best-seller ranking to an all-EV list for a second straight year. The B-segment/subcompact category emerged as the hottest segment, accounting for three of the top four sellers in October and five models within the broader top 20; this contrasts with OEM output, since 56% of new SUVs launched during the year exceeded 5 meters/197 inches — a disconnect between consumer demand for small vehicles and manufacturers' large-SUV offerings. Among individual best-sellers, Geely Xingyuan led with 50,190 registrations (up 14% YoY), followed by BYD Song at 30,772 (+6%), BYD Yuan Up at 28,514 (+44%, a record), Leapmotor A10 at 27,247, and Xiaomi Skynomad N-Series at 27,132 in its second month. The VW ID.Aura T6 reached the top-20 with 7,807 units for Tesla's Model Y (down 60% YoY) — though note that figure is the Aura T6's own volume; Tesla's overall decline was reported separately as a -60% drop to 7,807 units. At the manufacturer level, Leapmotor (+31%) and Xiaomi (+3%) were exceptions amid broad losses, while foreign brands such as Nissan (-70%) and Honda (-51%) also fell sharply; Nevo's +125% growth was attributed by the author to replacing its parent Changan brand (down 60%), not genuine sales gains. Brand share led with BYD at 17.2%, Geely second at 7.1%, Leapmotor third at 6.7%; group-level shares showed BYD leading at 21.9% and SAIC stable at 8%. These projections are the author's own expectations rather than verified forecasts, and several sales figures (e.g., Tesla Model Y) appear conflated in the source text.
items.title: China EV Market Share Hits Record 68% in October, Driven by Small BEVs and ICE Decline

items.summary: A free Datadog eBook addresses the challenge of identifying meaningful signals during latency spikes across hundreds of infrastructure metrics, proposing a framework for monitoring dynamic cloud-native environments with worked examples for Kubernetes and AWS Lambda. The framework instructs readers to separate work metrics (throughput, success rate, errors, latency) from resource metrics, reduce alert noise by paging on symptoms rather than causes, and apply the approach to both Kubernetes clusters and Lambda functions. A system design refresher segment contrasts Docker as a single-machine packaging tool that creates portable container images deployable via Docker Compose with Kubernetes as an orchestration platform managing deployment and maintenance across multiple machines, including automatic scaling, self-healing, high availability, traffic distribution, and update rollouts. The text also summarizes Redis's in-memory operation, describes Claude watermarking as a keyed function selecting valid word candidates to embed detectable signals, lists seven open-weights versus closed-model tradeoffs (fine-tuning, versioning, transparency, deployment, licensing, self-hosting, cost), explains Anthropic's intent to identify AI-generated text based on the author's understanding rather than official confirmation, and enumerates nine distributed systems patterns including replication, sharding, consistent hashing, pub/sub, circuit breaker, retry with backoff, leader election, quorum read/write, and saga. The watermarking explanation is explicitly attributed to personal interpretation, and no figures or quantitative data are provided.
items.title: Datadog Releases Monitoring eBook and Hosts Distributed Systems Refresher Covering Docker vs Kubernetes

items.summary: In Buea, capital of Cameroon's Southwest region, children displaced by the country's ongoing armed Anglophone conflict are resuming schooling but increasingly taking on market work to help their families survive. The crisis began in 2016 when teachers and lawyers protested over perceived marginalization of English-language education and common-law systems favoring French; this escalated into armed conflict between government forces and separatist groups seeking independence for the two English-speaking regions, commonly referred to as Ambazonia. UNHCR estimates that between 2.1 and 2.2 million people have been displaced due to the violence. At Buea's OIC Market, children from displaced families sell bleach, puff-puff, plantains, ginger, garlic, and oranges, particularly on weekends and before school. Fourteen-year-old Joy travels from Mutengene to Buea on weekends to sell sachets of bleach that her mother buys in bulk and repackages; she sells each for CFA 100 (about USD 0.17) with daily sales reaching CFA 10,000–15,000 (about USD 16.81–25.21). Fourteen-year-old Sidoine lost four years of schooling after her family fled Ekona when their house was burned; a well-wisher helped enroll her in Buea, though the family cannot permanently return to its farm. Younger children also contribute: twelve-year-old Michelle sells plantains while waiting for his mother from church, and Susan Achuagoh gives small quantities of oranges to sell while she stays at her stall after more than three years of interrupted schooling for her five children. Godiva Ndang epse Limene, Education and Partnerships Officer at Street Child UK-Cameroon, notes that prolonged exposure to armed violence may cause anxiety, difficulty concentrating, and social withdrawal, and warns that work consuming time needed for learning can affect cognitive, emotional, social, and physical development; she stresses that helping in a family business is not automatically child labor, with the distinction depending on age, activity nature and duration, risks involved, and whether it interferes with education, health, rest, or development. Education data cited by UNICEF from Regional Delegations of Basic Education figures dated September 2026 show that 223,749 children were completely out of school in the Northwest and Southwest regions, while 2,463 schools were non-operational—of which 2,005 were in the Northwest and 458 in the Southwest. Local partners including TeenAlive, FIED, SHUMAS, and AMEF support close to 100 Mobile Neighborhood Learning Corners and Satellite Learning Corners established in accessible locations such as village chiefs' homes, churches, schools, and community verandas; other interventions include school enrollment help, uniforms, learning materials, Teaching at the Right Level tutoring, Street Child's girls' resilience program with vocational training and mental health assistance, and FIFA Foundation-supported Play for Peace. Despite interruptions and added responsibilities, interviewed children retain ambitions—Eliot (14) wants to be an engineer, Sidoine hopes to study law though she worries about lost years, and Vickians (12), who sells miondo on weekends after fleeing Lebialem, studies computer science and aims to become a computer engineer. Southwest Governor Bernard Okalia Bilai stated at the start of the 2026–2027 academic year that authorities want children across the region equal access to education despite differences in school attendance between urban and rural communities.
items.title: Displaced Cameroon Children in Buea Balance Schooling with Market Work After a Decade of Anglophone Conflict
